\[
D = G_{\sigma} * I - G_{k\sigma} * I = (G_{\sigma} - G_{k\sigma}) * I
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G_{\sigma}\): A normalized Gaussian with standard deviation sigma
- \(k\): The ratio of the two sigmas

G is a normalized Gaussian. Both blurs keep the mean, so their difference is 0 in flat areas. The narrow blur keeps details that the wide one removes, so the difference holds the details between the two scales. For k near 1 it is close to (k - 1) sigma squared times the Laplacian of Gaussian, which is why it serves as a cheap blob and edge detector. Both Gaussians are truncated at 3 sigma.
